messages:
lina: kicking off a small canary for zephyr-lite-int8 on the /tools/structured route — after the recent qconfig tweak weve seen parse errors creep up to ~4.9% on our onboarding sample set.

lina: small example of the kind of output failing schema validation:
```
FYI: model thinks this field is optional
{"intent": "update_profile", "user_id": "u123", "attrs": [
  "email:\"x@ex.com\"",
], } trailing note about confidence
```

josiah: yep, two main nuisances: explanatory prefixes like `FYI:` and then trailing punctuation/commas in arrays/objects. also sometimes the model emits mid-stream clarifying sentences. naive json.loads blows up.

ben: proposal for a lightweight repair harness we can toggle per-canary:
1) strip-leading-prefixes: drop lines that match ^[A-Z]{2,}:.*$ (e.g. FYI:, NOTE:) up to first `{`.
2) token-split rejoiner: if we see lines ending in `...` or cut words, stitch them heuristically before parse.
3) pretty-parse attempt: try tolerant parser (json5-like) and reserialize to strict JSON.
4) chunked-append repair: if parse fails and the text looks like truncated object (starts with `{` but no closing `}`), try appending `}` (or `}}`) up to 3 times and reparse.
5) final fallback: wrap as {\"__raw\": \"...\"} and mark as wrapped so downstream ignores as tool invocation.

sophia: strong caution: repaired JSON must still validate against the tool schema. If repair yields JSON that fails schema, tag `repair.validated=false` and don't autopromote. We need telemetry keys: `repair.attempted`, `repair.method`, `repair.success`, `repair.validation` and `repair.kind`.

lina: current canary snapshot (last 30m): canary_count=1200, parse_fail_rate=0.049, repair_attempted=220, repair_success=95

deploy-bot: start-canary zephyr-lite-int8 -> job 11234 started. logs: https://ci/canary/11234 (monitoring)

josiah: small bash prototype for step 1+3 I used locally:
```bash
# strip leading caps-prefixes and attempt json5 parser via node
cat sample_output.txt | sed -n '1,200p' | awk 'BEGIN{p=0} /\{/ {p=1} {if(p) print}' | node -e '\nconst fs=require("fs")\nconst s=fs.readFileSync(0,\"utf8\")\ntry{const json=require(\"json5\").parse(s); console.log(JSON.stringify(json));}catch(e){console.error(\"parse fail\",e.message); process.exit(2)}\n'
```

ben: gotcha: chunked-append can create false positives for nested objects; only run it when the only imbalance is trailing braces (count('{') > count('}') by small amount) and no unmatched quotes heuristics trigger.

sophia: ops policy: do not enable auto-repair by default for Dedicated customers; expose an opt-in toggle at org-level and document rollback criteria (user-visible contract errors > 0.1% for 1h triggers rollback).

lina: plan: run an A/B for 4h comparing repair_mode=prettyparse vs repair_mode=chunked-append. metrics to collect: parse_fail_rate, repair_attempted, repair_success_rate, downstream_contract_errors, user_visible_anomalies.

josiah: will add unit tests for: trailing-commas-in-arrays, explanatory-prefix-lines, token-split-rejoin, truncated-object-append. will also add a small fuzz harness with quant-noise-ish variants.

ben: I'll instrument telemetry and add the repair.kind and repair.confidence (0.0-1.0) fields. also add a `repair.suspect` flag if the repaired object differs structurally from original predictions (keys added/removed).

deploy-bot: canary job 11234 health: all pods running, sampler active.

lina: assign follow-ups: josiah (tests + harness), ben (telemetry + heuristics), sophia (policy toggle + rollback), i'll run AB and gather results. will reconvene after 4h. :clock4:

josiah: on it. ping me if AB shows any contract regressions. :mag:
